title: Internal Hom of constant modules with finitely presented source
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $P,Q$ be $\Lambda$-modules. Assume $P$ is finitely presented, meaning that there are finite integers $a,b\geq0$ and an exact sequence $\Lambda^a\to\Lambda^b\to P\to0$. Use the constant module sheaves $\underline P,\underline Q,\underline\Lambda$ of [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor], and the ordinary sheaf Hom of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. The canonical $\underline\Lambda$-linear map
$$
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(P,Q)}\longrightarrow
\mathcal Hom_{\underline\Lambda}(\underline P,\underline Q)
$$
sending a locally represented constant linear map $f:P\to Q$ to the corresponding map of constant module sheaves is an isomorphism. The map is natural in $P,Q$ and uses the same constant linear map after restriction to any localized site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No finite generation of $Q$, finiteness of $\Lambda$, or hypothesis on points of $\mathcal C$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 093T, sites-modules-lemma-locally-constant, part (1), including its canonical map in the proof; restriction is the defining localization rule for sheaf Hom, Tag 0E8H, sites-modules-lemma-internal-hom-restriction.

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(P,Q)$, $F(M)=\underline M$, and $H(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\underline\Lambda|_U}(F(P)|_U,F(Q)|_U)$. By [lem-sf-local-module-hom-sheaf] this is a sheaf of sets; the identification with [def-pur-sheaf-hom] equips it with its sectionwise abelian-group and $\underline\Lambda$-module structures. For $f\in E$ define $c_U(f)=F(f)|_U$. The restriction rule of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] makes $c:\operatorname{const}(E)\to H$ a natural transformation. Write $\eta_M$ for the constant-module unit. The explicit construction [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] gives $F(f)_V(\eta_P(p))=\eta_Q(f(p))$. Thus $c_U(f+g)=c_U(f)+c_U(g)$ and $c_U(\lambda f)=\eta_\Lambda(\lambda)c_U(f)$: the corresponding global sheaf maps agree on the constant-presheaf unit by the displayed formula, so uniqueness in sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] makes those global maps equal, and restricting gives the asserted equalities on each slice. Consequently $c$ is, in particular, a morphism of presheaves of abelian groups.

source.place: Tag 093T, lemma-locally-constant (1), canonical comparison; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; Tag 0E8H, lemma-internal-hom-restriction

proof.text: The images of the $b$ standard basis vectors under $\Lambda^b\to P$ generate $P$: surjectivity says every $p$ is the image of a finite linear combination of those basis vectors. Hence $P$ is finitely generated, including $b=0$. Apply [lem-sf-constant-module-hom-locally-injective] with $M=P,N=Q$ and [lem-sf-constant-module-hom-locally-surjective] with the same modules. Their canonical presheaf comparison is precisely $c$, since both send $f$ to its induced constant-module map on every slice. The first lemma gives local injectivity, and the second uses exactly the given finite presentation of $P$ to give local surjectivity. Neither lemma asks that $Q$ be finitely generated or that $\Lambda$ be finite.

source.place: Tag 093T, lemma-locally-constant (1), finite-presentation comparison expanded through the existing local injectivity and local surjectivity lemmas

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] to the additive presheaf map $c$. It gives an isomorphism $c^\#: (\operatorname{const}E)^\#\to H^\#$ of abelian sheaves. Because $H$ is already a sheaf, the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies $H^\#$ with $H$: the identity of $H$ extends to a map $H^\#\to H$, inverse to its sheafification unit by uniqueness. The source is the underlying abelian sheaf of $F(E)$ by [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. We therefore obtain an additive sheaf isomorphism $\alpha:F(E)\to H$ characterized by $\alpha_U(\eta_E(f))=c_U(f)$. This factorization equation identifies the map with the canonical map of the statement, rather than merely giving an isomorphism between the two objects.

source.place: Tag 00WH, proposition-sheafification-adjoint; Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification, and Tag 00WN, lemma-mono-epi-sheaves, underlying the locally bijective criterion

proof.text: The local surjectivity in [lem-sf-constant-module-unit-locally-bijective], applied to $E$, represents any $s\in F(E)(U)$ locally by $\eta_E(f)$. For the constant ring presheaf, [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] says that the underlying set sheaf of $\underline\Lambda$ and its unit are the set sheafification of the constant underlying set. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] represents any $r\in\underline\Lambda(U)$ locally by $\eta_\Lambda(\lambda)$. Represent $s$ first and then represent the restrictions of $r$, giving a common covering by the transitivity axiom of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The scalar action of [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] extends the constant presheaf action. Therefore on this covering the computation in step 1 gives $\alpha(rs)=c(\lambda f)=\eta_\Lambda(\lambda)c(f)=r\alpha(s)$. Separatedness of $H$ gives this equality on $U$, so $\alpha$ is $\underline\Lambda$-linear. Its additive inverse is linear too: for $h=\alpha(s)$, the equality $\alpha(rs)=rh$ and injectivity of $\alpha_U$ imply $\alpha_U^{-1}(rh)=r\alpha_U^{-1}(h)$. Hence $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves. Empty covering sieves cause no exception, since sections of a sheaf on an object covered by the empty sieve are unique.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, explicit scalar compatibility; sites.tex Tag 00WK, local representatives

proof.text: For linear maps $u:P^\prime\to P$ and $v:Q\to Q^\prime$, with $P^\prime$ finitely presented when asserting the corresponding comparison is an isomorphism, both naturality composites on a constant section $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(P,Q)$ give $F(vfu)=F(v)\circ F(f)\circ F(u)$. Functoriality is the constant-presheaf functoriality followed by sheafification in [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. By local surjectivity of $\eta_E$ in [lem-sf-constant-module-unit-locally-bijective], every section is locally a constant section; separatedness of the target sheaf makes the two composites equal on every object. For localization at $U$, use [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction] for $P,Q,\Lambda,E$. Its comparisons preserve the units and send each constant linear map to the same linear map. By [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and relocalization [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], both $H|_U$ and the slice internal Hom assign to $(V\to U)$ the maps $F(P)|_V\to F(Q)|_V$, with exactly the same restrictions. Under these identifications both the restricted $\alpha$ and the slice comparison send $\eta_E(f)$ to $F(f)|_V$; local constant representatives and separatedness again make them equal. This proves the stated naturality and compatibility with every localized site without invoking any pullback assertion for an arbitrary morphism of topoi.
